para: A trade study asks which objectives trade and ends in a choice that can be defended; decision analysis Howard, 1988Keeney & Raiffa, 1993Parnell, 2016, model-based systems engineering Madni & Sievers, 2018, multidisciplinary design analysis and optimization Martins & Lambe, 2013 and multiobjective optimization Miettinen, 1999 are the forms that question takes. Answering it at the scale of a generated table calls for a recognized, rigorous and reproducible technique, which is what unsupervised learning offers: dimensionality reduction and kernel methods Jolliffe & Cadima, 2016Schölkopf et al., 1998 reduce a table to a structure a person can read, and data envelopment analysis Charnes et al., 1978 scores each design against the edge of the table. A method that finds trade-offs must then be fitted, and the convergence and performance of the fit rest on convex optimization and generalized geometric programming Boyd et al., 2007Hoburg & Abbeel, 2014. Figure 1 separates two uses of the optimization literature: as the solver beneath an unsupervised learning technique, and as a method of decision analysis. Table 1 places each family in its layer. The table summarizes the register of prior art in Appendix A.

HoroPCA. HoroPCA Chami et al., 2021 is the closest existing analog in setting: unsupervised, with a table in and coordinates out. It is the farthest in what is estimated: it extends the components of PCA to hyperbolic space with horospherical projections, maximizing a variance. This work fits the one-sided edge of a table and is not a PCA of any kind. We borrow that setting and the estimator interface of scikit-learn, and use PCA as a downstream step (Appendix B.11). In a prospectively specified test, on an embedding of ours, the authors’ code, at its defaults and one direction at a time, recovered the planted trade-offs only where they were the direction of largest spread; the tables are clean, so it demonstrates a mechanism and does not measure how often recovery succeeds (Appendix C).

Thresholds and ties. Three thresholds read an exponent, each a convention: at or below 10-12 it is numerically zero, not mathematically so; above 10-9 in the exact-maximum fit it is in the contending set of Definition 10; above the participation threshold (10-3), read at the fit temperature, it participates and carries an elasticity. They nest in size, and the last two read different fits. A member of the contending set below the participation threshold contends in the limit and carries no elasticity at the fit temperature. The stopping declaration. Each returned fit carries the levels it meets (Appendix B.4). For a sharp fit, certified means that the assignment is fixed, the residuals and the term gaps are within tolerance, no cell is empty and the margin is positive, so Corollary 2 bounds the remaining improvement with the cells held fixed and Proposition 3 applies to the exact minimizers the fit approximates. For a soft fit, certified means that the second-order test holds (Theorem 13), and stationary that the term gaps hold and the Hessian is not positive definite on the tangent space of the active face. Certified is a status at the returned point, set by tolerances, and the returned point is polished: at finite 
𝜏
τ each term’s refit is followed by Newton steps that close the gap the solver leaves (Appendix E.2); Proposition 3 and Theorem 13 hold at the exact point that the fit approximates. Whether a fit is stationary within tolerance, and so its status, is measured, not proved.

On the cubesat case of Section 7 (primary regime, 2,134 feasible designs), at K = 2 the margin, a gap between term scores, is 0.0003768, against a band 1/tau of 0.0088 and a median best-minus-second-best score of 0.352: a margin below the band puts at least one design within the band of a seam, here 37 of the 2,134. For the two-term split: the local optimality certified covers changes of the term scores under half the margin, about 47 times smaller than the band, so which term those 37 designs fall to is not a finding; the contending sets themselves hold under rounding-level jitter (Appendix B.7). In the parameters the same condition is the stable radius, 2.552e-05: the certificate covers moves of each term's exponents and reach under it.
Appendix G records what the results leave open.

The case is a fleet of identical 12U-class cubesats whose power, mass and attitude control are coupled, described by a SysML v2 system model in the repository (Appendix F). Its precedent is the CubeSat design problem among the applications of OpenMDAO Gray et al., 2019, which couples attitude, solar power, energy storage and communication to maximize the data downloaded; here the configurations are sampled and evaluated, not optimized. The problem is

A configuration swaps a part for one of its alternatives (swap: the wheel class, the tracker grade) and tunes a parameter of a part within a range (tune: panel span, battery capacity and the controller gains Kp and Kd). Every name is read from the system model; so are the ranges, which the view does not draw (Appendix F.1).

Each configuration is evaluated by the case’s oracle: the slew is integrated in Python, and every other attribute and the four feasibility verdicts are computed by the SysML v2 model’s calcs and requirements. Conditioning orients each attribute, shifts and scales it to unit log-spread and keeps the map invertible and the count: thirteen attributes make thirteen metrics. This conditioning centres each log-metric (the standard scaler). The fit temperature is selected by the rule of Section 5 (Figure 6).

The fit temperature is tau = 41.7: a fraction 0.098 of designs lies above V = 1 (the target is 0.10), the band 1/tau is 0.0240 and the effective sample size is 73.6 designs. The effective sample size is the inverse sum of squares of the support weights, the softmax weights of the designs in the fit: the designs the soft maximum weighs as if equally, so the exponents at the fit temperature rest on about that many of the 2,134 designs. The contending set holds with the target fraction halved or doubled (Appendix B.3).

Of 2,134 feasible cubesat designs, the nondominated set (on the conditioned metrics, larger is better) holds 236 on 4 attributes (settling time, pointing error, control effort and total mass) and 2,134 on all 13 (Appendix B.5; counts that hold over five regenerations of the data under rounding-level perturbation; a number that moves over them is printed as a range, Appendix B.7).

The package's checks for choosing K (Appendix B.10) point to K = 2 on the primary regime and the baseline regime, none deciding alone: the mean slack (in log V), read at the K = 1 temperature, drops most at K = 2 (0.08 and 0.05) and less at K = 3 (0.02 and 0.03), the largest drop read against the other two checks. The thinnest term holds 0.26 and 0.25 of the near-frontier designs at K = 2 and 0.06 and 0.06 at K = 3, the step where a thin term appears.

The K = 2 terms have contending sets (exact-maximum supports) of 8 and 7 metrics; peak slew power, absent from the K = 1 set, carries the largest exponent of term 1 (0.43). At the fit temperature total mass also carries 0.0064 on term 2, so it is drawn in that term's tension matrix without being in its contending set. The term shares are 0.74 and 0.26 for terms 1 and 2 (Appendix B.1).
Two regimes. The same pipeline on the baseline regime, whose gains were sampled over a lower range, separates the problem’s contribution from the gains’ (Appendix B.2).

Propose, predict, check. A regressor from configuration to chart coordinates predicts where proposals in the white space of the four-metric chart fall, and the proposals are then measured (Appendix B.6).

Applied after the K = 1 fit as constraints on the solution space, the six requirements exclude 178 of its 238 near-frontier designs jointly; one at a time: peak slew power 108, control effort 95, unit cost 64, fleet cost 57, total mass 12 and pointing error 8 (Appendix B.12).

With every design set conditioned as the fit of record is, removing the infeasible designs or imposing the four performance thresholds before the fit leaves the one-term contending set of the primary regime (seven metrics) unchanged and changes that of the baseline regime by at most two of its eight metrics (Appendix B.12).

The decision. The requirements and the fits cut 2,134 feasible designs to a shortlist of 28 that pass all six requirements and lie in the near-frontier band of both fits (Appendix B.14). On it the manufacturer and the operator pick the same fleet: 25 medium-wheel, medium-tracker satellites at 234,000 USD each, 5.85 M USD for the fleet and a coverage probability of 0.98. The unit cost falls and the coverage probability rises with the fleet size. The sponsor picks 4 small-wheel, medium-tracker satellites at 1.13 M USD, with a coverage probability of 0.46. What remains is the question the fit names, and it is the executives': how much fleet cost a gain in coverage probability is worth. Of the 17 shortlisted designs that no other beats on both, the fleet of 10 small-wheel, medium-tracker satellites at 2.88 M USD, with a coverage probability of 0.76, has the smallest larger shortfall on the two, each scaled from its best to its worst on the shortlist.

The picks’ levels lie inside the near-frontier band that the shortlist uses and do not rank them; the baseline’s level is outside it. The picks’ other design variables are in Appendix B.14.

The decision and Table 3 are reproduced from the primary regime’s table of the data of record by two calls. The fits are case.k_fits; the shortlist, the picks and the table are decision of the paper’s findings generator. Appendix H.3 gives the commands; outside the environment of record values differ in the last digits (Appendix H.2). What no rerun supplies is the executives’ answer.

Limits. The fitted reference surface is log-convex, and one term is tangent at one place and conservative off it. The exponents and elasticities are features of the conditioned table: they depend on the conditioning, describe how the sampled designs trade and not a causal exchange that changing a variable would reproduce, and a small sample determines them weakly. Designed samples, such as grids, are not independent observations: the exponents describe the sample and are not estimates with a sampling error. The certificate is local, and that the fit holds for designs outside the table, or supports a decision, is a further claim that needs its own validation. The case’s hardware values are illustrative and its costs a lower bound on a full costing; the case has no schedule, no payload and a flat launch price, and the coverage probability’s two constants are mission assumptions the operator supplies (Appendix G). Trade-offs the sampling never exercised cannot appear, and white space in the chart is an opportunity only where the trade space is log-convex around it, which the data cannot prove.

Every figure, table and reported number comes from a call into a tested module. The pinned toolchain, the environment of record and the commands are in Appendix H. To run your own table, supply the configurations, the attributes and a conditioning rule, and make the same calls; the docsite’s Getting started page is where to begin.
